qe: If the price of a commodity is increased by 25%, by what percentage should its consumption be decreased so that the expenditure of the commodity stays the same?
qh: यदि किसी वस्तु के मूल्य में 25% की वृद्धि होती है, तो उसके उपभोग में कितने प्रतिशत की कमी की जानी चाहिए ताकि वस्तु पर होने वाला खर्च समान रहे?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Price me increase $= 25\% = \frac{1}{4}$.
Initial Price : New Price $= 4 : 5$.
Hum jante hain ki $\text{Expenditure} = \text{Price} \times \text{Consumption}$.
Expenditure constant rakhne ke liye consumption ka ratio price ka ulta hoga:
Consumption ratio $= 5 : 4$.
Consumption me kami $= 5 - 4 = 1$ unit (5 ke base par).
Percentage decrease $= \frac{1}{5} \times 100\% = 20.0\%$.
Atah sahi vikalp  20.0% hai.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Initial expenditure $= 100$.
Price $25\%$ badhne ke baad cost $= 125$.
Kharcha 100 par wapas laane ke liye cut $= 125 - 100 = 25$.
125 ke base par percentage cut:
$= \frac{25}{125} \times 100\% = \frac{1}{5} \times 100\% = 20.0\%$.
Atah sahi uttar '20.0%' hai.

Exam point: pratishat ka hisaab - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: The cost of onions per kg is increased by 200%. A housewife reduces her consumption of onions by 60%. By what percentage does her expenditure on onions increase or decrease?
qh: प्याज के प्रति किलोग्राम मूल्य में 200% की वृद्धि होती है। एक गृहिणी प्याज के अपने उपभोग में 60% की कमी करती है। प्याज पर उसके खर्च में कितने प्रतिशत की वृद्धि या कमी होती है?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Price: $200\%$ increase ka matlab price $(1 + 2) = 3$ guna ho gaya $\implies$ Price ratio $= 1 : 3$.
Consumption: $60\%$ kami $= \frac{3}{5} \implies$ Consumption ratio $= 5 : (5 - 3) = 5 : 2$.
$\text{Expenditure} = \text{Price} \times \text{Consumption}$.
Initial Expenditure : New Expenditure $= (1 \times 5) : (3 \times 2) = 5 : 6$.
Expenditure me increase $= 6 - 5 = 1$ unit (5 ke base par).
Percentage increase $= \frac{1}{5} \times 100\% = 20\%$ (Increases, 20%).
Atah sahi vikalp  Increases, 20% hai.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Initial expenditure $= 100$.
Price $200\%$ badhne ke baad intermediate cost $= 100 + 200 = 300$.
Consumption $60\%$ ghatne par new expenditure $= 300 - (60\% \text{ of } 300) = 300 - 180 = 120$.
Net change over base $100 = 120 - 100 = +20\%$ (Increases, 20%).
Atah sahi uttar 'Increases, 20%' hai.

Exam point: pratishat ka hisaab - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: The cost of wheat is increased by 20% but its consumption is decreased by 25%. Find the percentage increase or decrease in the expenditure of money.
qh: गेहूं के मूल्य में 20% की वृद्धि होती है लेकिन इसके उपभोग में 25% की कमी आती है। खर्च में होने वाली प्रतिशत वृद्धि या कमी ज्ञात कीजिए।
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Price ($+20\% = \frac{1}{5}$): ratio $= 5 : 6$.
Consumption ($-25\% = -\frac{1}{4}$): ratio $= 4 : 3$.
$\text{Expenditure} = \text{Price} \times \text{Consumption}$.
Initial Expenditure : New Expenditure $= (5 \times 4) : (6 \times 3) = 20 : 18 = 10 : 9$.
Expenditure me kami $= 10 - 9 = 1$ unit (10 ke base par).
Percentage decrease $= \frac{1}{10} \times 100\% = 10\%$ decrease.
Atah sahi vikalp  10% decrease hai.

Method 2 (Successive Formula):
Net Change $= a + b + \frac{ab}{100}$
Yahan $a = +20\%$ aur $b = -25\%$:
$= 20 - 25 + \frac{20 \times (-25)}{100} = -5 - 5 = -10\%$ (10% decrease).
Atah sahi uttar '10% decrease' hai.

Exam point: pratishat ka hisaab - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: When the price of an article increased by 20%, a family reduced its consumption in such a way that the expenditure on it was only 8% more. By what percentage has the family reduced the consumption of the article?
qh: जब किसी वस्तु के मूल्य में 20% की वृद्धि हुई, तो एक परिवार ने इसके उपभोग में इस प्रकार कमी की कि इस पर होने वाला खर्च केवल 8% ही बढ़ा। परिवार ने वस्तु के उपभोग में कितने प्रतिशत की कमी की?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
$\text{Expenditure} = \text{Price} \times \text{Consumption} \implies \text{Consumption} = \frac{\text{Expenditure}}{\text{Price}}$.
Price ratio ($+20\%$): $100 : 120 = 5 : 6$.
Expenditure ratio ($+8\%$): $100 : 108 = 25 : 27$.
Consumption ratio $= \frac{25}{5} : \frac{27}{6} = 5 : 4.5 = 10 : 9$.
Consumption me kami $= 10 - 9 = 1$ unit (10 ke base par).
Percentage reduction $= \frac{1}{10} \times 100\% = 10\%$.
Atah sahi vikalp  10% hai.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Initial expenditure $= 100$.
Price badhne ke baad cost $= 120$.
Target expenditure $= 108$.
Consumption me cut required $= 120 - 108 = 12$.
120 ke base par percentage cut:
$= \frac{12}{120} \times 100\% = 10\%$.
Atah sahi uttar '10%' hai.

Exam point: pratishat ka hisaab - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: The price of petrol is increased by 25%. A person wants to increase his expenditure by 15% only. By what percentage should he decrease his consumption?
qh: पेट्रोल के मूल्य में 25% की वृद्धि होती है। एक व्यक्ति अपने खर्च में केवल 15% की वृद्धि करना चाहता है। उसे अपने उपभोग में कितने प्रतिशत की कमी करनी चाहिए?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Price ratio: $100 : 125 = 4 : 5$.
Expenditure ratio: $100 : 115 = 20 : 23$.
Consumption ratio $= \frac{\text{Expenditure}}{\text{Price}} = \frac{20}{4} : \frac{23}{5} = 5 : 4.6 = 25 : 23$.
Consumption me kami $= 25 - 23 = 2$ units (25 par).
Percentage decrease $= \frac{2}{25} \times 100\% = 8\%$.
Atah sahi vikalp  8% hai.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Initial Base $= 100$.
Price badhkar ho gayi $= 125$.
Allowed expenditure $= 115$.
Kami kitni karni hogi $= 125 - 115 = 10$.
Badhe hue rate 125 ke base par percentage decrease:
$= \frac{10}{125} \times 100\% = \frac{2}{25} \times 100\% = 8\%$.
Atah sahi uttar '8%' hai.

Exam point: pratishat ka hisaab - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: The price of sugar is decreased by 20% and therefore a household increased the consumption of sugar by 15 kg to keep the expenditure same. What was the earlier consumption?
qh: चीनी के मूल्य में 20% की कमी आती है और इसलिए एक परिवार खर्च को समान रखने के लिए चीनी की खपत में 15 किग्रा की वृद्धि कर देता है। पहले की खपत कितनी थी?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Price decrease $= 20\% = \frac{1}{5}$.
Price ratio $= 5 : 4$.
Expenditure same rakhne ke liye consumption ka ratio price ka ulta hoga:
Consumption ratio $= 4 : 5$.
Consumption me badhav $= 5 - 4 = 1$ unit.
Given: 1 unit $= 15\text{ kg}$.
Earlier consumption = 4 units $= 4 \times 15 = 60\text{ kg}$.
Atah sahi vikalp  60 kg hai.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Base expenditure $= 100$.
Price drop hone ke baad $= 80$.
Wapas 100 par aane ke liye consumption badhana hoga $= 100 - 80 = 20$.
Percentage increase in consumption $= \frac{20}{80} = \frac{1}{4}$.
$\frac{1}{4}$ of original consumption $= 15\text{ kg} \implies \text{Original Consumption} = 15 \times 4 = 60\text{ kg}$.
Atah sahi uttar '60 kg' hai.

Exam point: diye gaye tathyon ka sahi milan - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: If the price of rice is reduced by 20%, it allows a person to buy 5 kg more rice for ₹1,200. The reduced rate of rice per kg is:
qh: यदि चावल के मूल्य में 20% की कमी होती है, तो यह एक व्यक्ति को ₹1,200 में 5 किग्रा अधिक चावल खरीदने की अनुमति देता है। चावल का घटा हुआ मूल्य प्रति किग्रा क्या है?
e:
Method 1 (Direct Savings Method):
₹1,200 par total bachat $= 20\% \text{ of } 1200 = \frac{20}{100} \times 1200 = ₹240$.
Is ₹240 ki bachat ki wajah se hi 5 kg extra rice milti hai.
Reduced Rate per kg $= \frac{₹240}{5\text{ kg}} = ₹48\text{ per kg}$.
Atah sahi vikalp  ₹48 hai.

Method 2 (Ratio Method):
Price ratio: $20\% = \frac{1}{5} \implies 5 : 4$.
Consumption ratio $= 4 : 5$.
Consumption increase $= 5 - 4 = 1$ unit $= 5\text{ kg}$.
New total consumption = 5 units $= 5 \times 5 = 25\text{ kg}$.
Reduced rate $= \frac{\text{Total Amount}}{\text{New Consumption}} = \frac{1200}{25} = ₹48\text{ per kg}$.
Atah sahi uttar '₹48' hai.

Exam point: diye gaye tathyon ka sahi milan - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: A reduction of 20% in the price of detergent powder enables a buyer to obtain 4 kg more for ₹960. The original price of the detergent powder per kg is:
qh: डिटर्जेंट पाउडर के मूल्य में 20% की कमी एक खरीदार को ₹960 में 4 किग्रा अधिक प्राप्त करने में सक्षम बनाती है। डिटर्जेंट पाउडर का मूल मूल्य प्रति किग्रा क्या है?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Price ratio: $20\% = \frac{1}{5} \implies 5 : 4$.
Consumption ratio $= 4 : 5$.
Increase in consumption $= 5 - 4 = 1$ unit.
Given: 1 unit $= 4\text{ kg}$.
Original consumption = 4 units $= 4 \times 4 = 16\text{ kg}$.
Original Price per kg $= \frac{\text{Total Money}}{\text{Original Consumption}} = \frac{960}{16} = ₹60\text{ per kg}$.
Atah sahi vikalp  ₹60 hai.

Method 2 (100-Base / Reduced to Original Method):
₹960 par $20\%$ bachat $= 0.20 \times 960 = ₹192$.
Reduced price per kg $= \frac{192}{4} = ₹48\text{ per kg}$.
Reduced price original price ka $80\%$ hai:
$80\% = 48 \implies 1\% = 0.6 \implies 100\% = ₹60\text{ per kg}$.
Atah sahi uttar '₹60' hai.

Exam point: diye gaye tathyon ka sahi milan - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: A reduction of 25% in the price of wheat enables a person to buy 6 kg more for ₹600. What is the original price per kg?
qh: गेहूं के मूल्य में 25% की कमी एक व्यक्ति को ₹600 में 6 किग्रा अधिक खरीदने में सक्षम बनाती है। गेहूं का मूल मूल्य प्रति किग्रा क्या है?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Price ratio: $25\% = \frac{1}{4} \implies 4 : 3$.
Consumption ratio $= 3 : 4$.
Increase in consumption $= 4 - 3 = 1$ unit.
Given: 1 unit $= 6\text{ kg}$.
Original consumption = 3 units $= 3 \times 6 = 18\text{ kg}$.
Original Price per kg $= \frac{600}{18} = \frac{100}{3} = ₹33.33\text{ per kg}$.
Atah sahi vikalp  ₹33.33 hai.

Method 2 (Direct Savings Method):
₹600 par $25\%$ bachat $= \frac{1}{4} \times 600 = ₹150$.
Reduced price per kg $= \frac{150}{6} = ₹25\text{ per kg}$.
Original Price $= \frac{\text{Reduced Price}}{1 - 0.25} = \frac{25}{0.75} = \frac{100}{3} = ₹33.33\text{ per kg}$.
Atah sahi uttar '₹33.33' hai.

Exam point: diye gaye tathyon ka sahi milan - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: If the price of a pen decreases by 20%, then a person can buy 4 more pens for ₹160. What is the new price (in ₹) of each pen?
qh: यदि एक पेन के मूल्य में 20% की कमी होती है, तो एक व्यक्ति ₹160 में 4 पेन अधिक खरीद सकता है। प्रत्येक पेन का नया मूल्य (₹ में) क्या है?
e:
Method 1 (Direct Savings Method):
₹160 par $20\%$ ki bachat $= \frac{20}{100} \times 160 = ₹32$.
Is bache hue ₹32 me 4 extra pen aate hain.
New Price of each pen $= \frac{₹32}{4} = ₹8$.
Atah sahi vikalp  ₹8 hai.

Method 2 (Ratio Method):
Price ratio: $5 : 4$.
Quantity ratio: $4 : 5$.
Quantity me increase $= 5 - 4 = 1$ unit $= 4\text{ pens}$.
New total quantity = 5 units $= 5 \times 4 = 20\text{ pens}$.
New Price per pen $= \frac{160}{20} = ₹8$.
Atah sahi uttar '₹8' hai.

Exam point: diye gaye tathyon ka sahi milan - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: A 20% decrease in the cost of flour enables a consumer to purchase an additional 4 kg for ₹480. What was the initial price per kg of the flour?
qh: आटे के मूल्य में 20% की कमी होने से एक उपभोक्ता ₹480 में 4 किग्रा अधिक आटा खरीद सकता है। आटे का प्रारंभिक मूल्य प्रति किग्रा क्या था?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Price me kami $= 20\% = \frac{1}{5}$.
Price ka ratio $= 5 : 4$.
Expenditure same rakhne ke liye consumption ka ratio price ka ulta hoga:
Consumption ratio $= 4 : 5$.
Consumption me badhav $= 5 - 4 = 1$ unit.
Given: 1 unit $= 4\text{ kg}$.
Initial consumption = 4 units $= 4 \times 4 = 16\text{ kg}$.
Initial price per kg $= \frac{\text{Total Money}}{\text{Initial Consumption}} = \frac{480}{16} = ₹30\text{ per kg}$.
Atah sahi vikalp  ₹30 hai.

Method 2 (Direct Savings Method):
₹480 par total savings $= 20\% \text{ of } 480 = \frac{20}{100} \times 480 = ₹96$.
Is ₹96 ki wajah se 4 kg extra aata milta hai.
Reduced price per kg $= \frac{96}{4} = ₹24\text{ per kg}$.
Kyunki reduced price original price ka $80\%$ hai:
Original Price $= \frac{24}{0.80} = ₹30\text{ per kg}$.
Atah sahi uttar '₹30' hai.

Exam point: diye gaye tathyon ka sahi milan - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: The reduction of 20% in the price of salt enables a person to buy 4 kg more for ₹320. The reduced price of salt per kg (in ₹) is:
qh: नमक के मूल्य में 20% की कमी होने पर एक व्यक्ति ₹320 में 4 किग्रा अधिक नमक खरीद सकता है। नमक का घटा हुआ मूल्य प्रति किग्रा (₹ में) क्या है?
e:
Method 1 (Direct Savings Method):
₹320 par $20\%$ ki bachat $= \frac{20}{100} \times 320 = ₹64$.
Is bachat se 4 kg extra salt milti hai.
Reduced price per kg $= \frac{₹64}{4\text{ kg}} = ₹16\text{ per kg}$.
Atah sahi vikalp  ₹16 hai.

Method 2 (Ratio Method):
Price ratio: $20\% = \frac{1}{5} \implies 5 : 4$.
Consumption ratio $= 4 : 5$.
Consumption increase $= 5 - 4 = 1$ unit $= 4\text{ kg}$.
New total consumption = 5 units $= 5 \times 4 = 20\text{ kg}$.
Reduced rate per kg $= \frac{320}{20} = ₹16\text{ per kg}$.
Atah sahi uttar '₹16' hai.

Exam point: diye gaye tathyon ka sahi milan - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: A reduction of 25% in the price of bananas enables a customer to buy 4 more bananas for ₹60. What is the reduced price of bananas per dozen (in ₹)?
qh: केले के मूल्य में 25% की कमी एक ग्राहक को ₹60 में 4 केले अधिक खरीदने में सक्षम बनाती है। प्रति दर्जन केले का घटा हुआ मूल्य (₹ में) क्या है?
e:
Method 1 (Direct Savings Method):
₹60 par total bachat $= 25\% \text{ of } 60 = \frac{1}{4} \times 60 = ₹15$.
Is ₹15 me 4 extra bananas milte hain.
Reduced price per banana $= \frac{₹15}{4}$.
1 dozen me 12 bananas hote hain, isliye:
Reduced price per dozen $= \frac{15}{4} \times 12 = 15 \times 3 = ₹45$.
Atah sahi vikalp  ₹45 hai.

Method 2 (Ratio Method):
Price ratio: $25\% = \frac{1}{4} \implies 4 : 3$.
Quantity ratio $= 3 : 4$.
Increase in quantity $= 4 - 3 = 1$ unit $= 4\text{ bananas}$.
New quantity = 4 units $= 4 \times 4 = 16\text{ bananas}$.
Reduced price for 16 bananas $= ₹60$.
Reduced price for 1 dozen (12 bananas) $= \frac{60}{16} \times 12 = \frac{15}{4} \times 12 = ₹45$.
Atah sahi uttar '₹45' hai.

Exam point: diye gaye tathyon ka sahi milan - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: A reduction of 25% in the price of sugar enables a person to buy 4 kg more for ₹300. What is the original price per kg?
qh: चीनी के मूल्य में 25% की कमी एक व्यक्ति को ₹300 में 4 किग्रा अधिक चीनी खरीदने में सक्षम बनाती है। चीनी का मूल मूल्य प्रति किग्रा क्या है?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Price ratio: $25\% = \frac{1}{4} \implies 4 : 3$.
Consumption ratio $= 3 : 4$.
Consumption increase $= 4 - 3 = 1$ unit.
Given: 1 unit $= 4\text{ kg}$.
Original consumption = 3 units $= 3 \times 4 = 12\text{ kg}$.
Original price per kg $= \frac{\text{Total Money}}{\text{Original Consumption}} = \frac{300}{12} = ₹25\text{ per kg}$.
Atah sahi vikalp  ₹25.00 hai.

Method 2 (Direct Savings Method):
₹300 par $25\%$ bachat $= \frac{1}{4} \times 300 = ₹75$.
Reduced rate per kg $= \frac{75}{4} = ₹18.75\text{ per kg}$.
Reduced price original price ka $75\%$ ($0.75$) hai:
Original Price $= \frac{18.75}{0.75} = \frac{1875}{75} = ₹25\text{ per kg}$.
Atah sahi uttar '₹25.00' hai.

Exam point: diye gaye tathyon ka sahi milan - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.
